title: When the Will Wakes Anew
premise: True-crime podcaster Zephyrine Almeida built a career closing cases no one else could, but the murder of a small-town archivist—dead forty years, case never opened—arrives on his desk as a confession letter postmarked one day after the victim's funeral. Following the letter's clues, Zephyrine discovers a coded ledger hidden in the town library's catalog system, one that names a respected judge among those who buried the crime. As the statute of limitations ticks down and someone begins erasing witnesses, Zephyrine must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the letter's author: the judge's daughter, who has loved him since their college years. In the end, Zephyrine broadcasts the decoded ledger in his final episode, forcing a confession before the law can intervene—but at the cost of the woman he loves and the anonymity that kept him alive.
about_author: August Dunmore is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing confessions before writing any of their own. They live off-grid in coastal Maine, where they research cold cases by lantern light and refuse to own a telephone.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Almeida receives an anonymous confession letter for a forty-year-old murder, postmarked the day after the victim's funeral. His producer warns him the case is radioactive; his pride won't let him refuse. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by unease—the letter knows things only the killer could know.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Quiet Room
chapters.summary: Zephyrine travels to Graywater Hollow and walks through the archive where victim Edith Marlowe worked, finding her personal effects sealed in evidence boxes never opened. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: reverent curiosity curdling into anger at how thoroughly the town chose to forget.

chapters.title: A Town That Buries Twice
chapters.summary: Interviews with elderly residents reveal a wall of polite silence; everyone remembers Edith, no one remembers anything useful. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: loneliness of the outsider, punctuated by one widow's whispered warning to leave before the anniversary.

chapters.title: The Letter's Second Voice
chapters.summary: Forensic analysis shows the confession contains two handwriting styles—one confessing, one correcting details. Someone else edited the killer's words. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: exhilaration of a real lead colliding with dread that he's being steered.

chapters.title: Dewey Decimal Ghosts
chapters.summary: Zephyrine notices the confession quotes call numbers verbatim and begins mapping them against the library's old catalog, suspecting a hidden index. POV: alternating Zephyrine and letters from Edith's journal. Emotional beat: the intimacy of reading a dead woman's voice.

chapters.title: Judge Aldous Vane
chapters.summary: The ledger trail points toward Judge Aldous Vane, who was town prosecutor when Edith died and closed the file without charges. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: cold recognition that power, not incompetence, buried this case.

chapters.title: Miriam
chapters.summary: Zephyrine encounters Miriam Vane, the judge's daughter, at a memorial service—and recognizes her from college, from before either of them had names worth hiding. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: old love resurfacing like a bruise he'd forgotten pressing.

chapters.title: What Miriam Kept
chapters.summary: Miriam privately admits she mailed the confession after finding her father's papers, but insists she doesn't know who killed Edith—only that her father protected someone. POV: Miriam. Emotional beat: guilt warring with filial loyalty, and terror of what Zephyrine's return means for her heart.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Decoding the catalog cipher, Zephyrine finds the ledger: payments logged across decades to keep witnesses quiet, each entry keyed to a shelf number. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: triumph sharpening into fear—the ledger names living people.

chapters.title: First Erasure
chapters.summary: The widow who warned Zephyrine dies suddenly, ruled natural causes, hours after he interviewed her. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: grief and self-blame; the case has started costing lives again.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Zephyrine learns a technicality will permanently seal the case in nineteen days unless new evidence forces action. He records an episode teaser to flush out opposition. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: gambler's resolve masking exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Producer's Doubt
chapters.summary: His producer confronts him: the teaser got downloads but also threats, and she found gaps in Zephyrine's own past he's never explained. POV: producer Dana Okafor. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by suspicion—who is Zephyrine really?

chapters.title: Shelf 411
chapters.summary: Following ledger entry 411, Zephyrine retrieves a hidden envelope in the library stacks containing Edith's final letter naming her killer by initial only: 'A.V.' POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: vertigo—the initials match both the judge and, impossibly, someone closer.

chapters.title: Two Sets of Initials
chapters.summary: Zephyrine realizes 'A.V.' could be Aldous Vane—or Aldous's brother, Amias Vane, the town's beloved retired sheriff who was first on scene in 1984. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the sick drop of realizing the protector may be the murderer.

chapters.title: Amias Confesses, Sort Of
chapters.summary: Confronted, Sheriff Amias admits he covered up the death but claims Edith died accidentally during a confrontation about the ledger, and that Aldous forced the burial. POV: Amias. Emotional beat: a good man's lifetime of shame finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Miriam's Choice
chapters.summary: Miriam offers Zephyrine her father's private files if he agrees to leave Amias out of the story—an ultimatum that puts justice and love on opposite scales. POV: Miriam. Emotional beat: heartbreak of asking the man she loves to settle for half a truth.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Fire
chapters.summary: The archive burns overnight, destroying Edith's remaining effects; Zephyrine barely escapes and realizes someone knew exactly which boxes mattered. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into certainty—he's close enough to be worth killing.

chapters.title: What Zephyrine Buried
chapters.summary: Dana's digging surfaces Zephyrine's secret: he is Edith Marlowe's grandnephew, and his entire podcasting identity was built to get near this case. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as devotion; she must decide whether to expose or stand by him.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, One Episode
chapters.summary: With the statute expiring, Zephyrine and Dana assemble the full broadcast: ledger, cipher, recordings, and Edith's letter. Miriam must decide whether to hand over her father's files on air. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: quiet, terrified commitment—no way back.

chapters.title: The Last Broadcast
chapters.summary: Zephyrine airs the episode live from the courthouse steps; mid-broadcast, Judge Aldous Vane arrives and confesses—not to killing Edith, but to burying his brother's crime for forty years. Amias surrenders beside him. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: catharsis and hollow victory intertwined.

chapters.title: After the Statute
chapters.summary: Both brothers face obstruction charges; Edith's case is formally reopened posthumously. Miriam, shattered by her family's ruin, tells Zephyrine she cannot love the man who dismantled her father. POV: Miriam. Emotional beat: mourning a future that justice made impossible.

chapters.title: When the Will Wakes Anew
chapters.summary: Months later, Zephyrine releases his final episode—a reading of Edith's own words—and retires the podcast, visiting her grave under his real name for the first time. Justice came outside the law, love died against duty, and identity, once hidden, is finally claimed. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; the case is closed, and so is he.
